He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. He was selected 54th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]], and played briefly for the Sixers. Shayok represented the South Sudan national team in the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]] and the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. ==Early life== Shayok was born in [[Ottawa]], Ontario, to Sudanese father Makur and mother Helena. Makur played basketball at the [[University of Dayton]] (1990-92)). Marial has four siblings, including two who played college basketball in the [[NCAA]]. His sister, Yar, played for the [[University of Detroit Mercy]], then signed with a professional team in France, while his older brother Shayok played at the [[IMG Academy]] and later at [[Bradley University]]. He also played basketball professionally in South America. {{cite news |last1=Baines |first1=Tim |title=Marial Shayok follows family tradition after landing a scholarship to Marquette University |url=https://ottawasun.com/2013/11/08/marial-shayok-follows-family-tradition/wcm/7d9f3981-e1ba-432f-89b0-1eb685dda317 |access-date=April 5, 2019 |work=[[Ottawa Sun]] |date=November 8, 2013}} Shayok started playing basketball at the age of seven, sometimes on the playgrounds, sometimes at the YMCA. Growing up, his favorite players were [[Michael Jordan]], [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Kevin Durant]], [[Penny Hardaway]], and [[Dwyane Wade]]. ==High school career== Shayok first attended and played basketball for three seasons for [[St. Patrick's High School (Ottawa)|St. Patrick’s High School]] in Ottawa, Canada.[https://virginiasports.com/player/marial-shayok/ "Marial Shayok,"] Virginia Sports. He then attended [[Blair Academy]] in [[Blairstown, New Jersey]], where Shayok played for two seasons while coached by Joe Mantegna. As a junior in 2012-13, he averaged 15 points, 6 rebounds, and 4 assists per game, He was named New Jersey Prep All-State and All-Mid Atlantic Prep League First-Team. As a senior in 2013-14, he averaged 15 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists per game, He was a First Team All-Prep selection by ''The Star-Ledger'', named the New Jersey Prep Player of the Year, and named New Jersey Prep All-State and All-Mid Atlantic Prep League First-Team .{{cite news |title=Boys basketball: Marial Shayok of Blair Academy commits to Marquette |url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-8399809458166563350/boys-basketball-marial-shayok-of-blair-academy-commits-to-marquette/ |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=The Star-Ledger |date=October 18, 2013}} Coming out of high school, Shayok signed with [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], but he never played for the team.{{cite news |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=What's this about Marial Shayok's very lofty 50-40-90 goal? |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/01/23/iowa-state-basketball-marial-shayok-surpass-cyclones-expectations-virginia/2644599002/ |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=January 23, 2019}} ==College career== ===Virginia=== As a freshman at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], Shayok averaged 3.8 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. The following season, he averaged 4.3 points and 1.9 rebounds per game, while shooting 49.2% from the field and 43.6% from 3-point range.{{cite news |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=Virginia transfer Shayok hoping to thrive in Iowa State's system next season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2018/01/16/virginia-transfer-shayok-hoping-thrive-iowa-states-system-next-season/1034395001/ |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=January 16, 2018}} Shayok posted 8.9 points and 2.4 rebounds per game for the Cavaliers as a junior, shooting 44 percent from the field and 33 percent from 3-point range. He scored 23 points in Virginia's victory in the first round of the NCAA Tournament against the [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington Seahawks]]. Following the season, Shayok opted to transfer and signed with [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] on April 19, 2017.{{cite news |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=Iowa State hoops lands Virginia transfer Marial Shayok |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2017/04/20/iowa-state-basketball-marial-shayok-transfer-virginia/100682812/ |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=April 19, 2017}} ===Iowa State=== [[File:2018.IowaStateGrad.jpg|thumb|Shayok at his 2019 Iowa State graduation]] Playing for Iowa State, Shayok scored 24 points in a 77–60 win over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] on January 5, 2019.{{cite news |title=Virginia transfer Shayok flourishing for Iowa State |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-transfer-shayok-flourishing-for-iowa-state/article_b19cd368-12c8-11e9-903d-8b4b550a7017.html |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=The Daily Progress |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 7, 2019}} On January 7, Shayok was named [[Big 12]] Player of the Week.{{cite news |last1=Visser |first1=Ben |title=Marial Shayok, the Big 12's leading scorer, personifies gym-rat mentality at Iowa State |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowa-state-cyclones/marial-shayok-iowa-state-basketball-virginia-transfer-big-12-leading-scorer-stats-20190107 |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |date=January 7, 2019}} In the semifinals of the Big 12 Conference tournament, the redshirt senior hit a pair of big 3-pointers in the final two minutes to help five-seed Iowa State defeat top seed Kansas State 63–59. Shayok finished with a game-high 21 points, helping the Cyclones battle back from a five-point deficit with 2 minutes, and 47 seconds remaining. None were bigger than the final two shots Shayok hit.{{cite news |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=A look at Marial Shayok's two big shots that helped Iowa State to the Big 12 title game|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2019/03/15/iowa-state-cyclones-marial-shayok-big-12-tournament-kansas-state/3172799002/ |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=March 15, 2019}} On March 16, in the finals of the Big 12 Conference tournament, Shayok scored 15 points in a 78–66 win over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and was named the [[Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] MVP to add to being named First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].{{cite news |title=Iowa State's Shayok All-Big 12 first-team |url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/basketball/iowa-state-s-shayok-all-big-first-team/article_ba48236a-d0f5-5f63-bd6f-b5f2cdceb69a.html |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=March 10, 2019 |archive-date=March 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329160558/https://wcfcourier.com/sports/basketball/iowa-state-s-shayok-all-big-first-team/article_ba48236a-d0f5-5f63-bd6f-b5f2cdceb69a.html |url-status=dead }} On day two of the 2019 [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], Shayok scored 37 points, including a three-pointer to force overtime for his team, as well as the game-winning shot in OT. He was 7-of-9 from three-point range and also had 7 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Parsons |first1=Brian |title=Marial steals the show at the PIT |url=https://www.wavy.com/sports/local-sports/marial-shayok-steals-the-show-at-the-pit/1937751510 |access-date=April 18, 2019 |work=[[WAVY-TV]] |date=April 18, 2019}} He was later named as part of the PIT All-Tournament Team. For the season, he averaged 18.7 points (2nd in the conference), 4.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 2.1 three-pointers (6th) per game, shooting 49.6% (2nd) from the field, 38.6% from three-point range (8th), and 87.8% (2nd; 18th in the NCAA) from the free throw line.[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/marial-shayok-1.html "Marial Shayok,"] Sports Reference. Shayok was the only player in the US who averaged 18.5 points while shooting at least 49% from the field, 38% on three-pointers, and 87% at the free throw line.[https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/marial-shayok/9875 "Marial Shayok,"] Cyclones. He was named an [[Associated Press]] [[All-America]] Honorable Mention, a [[Julius Erving Award]] finalist (Small Forward of the Year), and an All-Big 12 First-Team selection. ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2020)=== Shayok was selected with the 54th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite news |last1=Naso |first1=Josh |title=Sixers draft Iowa State's Marial Shayok with 54th overall pick |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/06/21/sixers-draft-iowa-states-marial-shayok-with-54th-overall-pick/ |access-date=August 28, 2021 |work=Sixers Wire |date=June 21, 2019}} On July 7, 2019, the 76ers announced that they had signed Shayok to a [[two-way contract]], meaning he would split time between the 76ers and their G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-shayok-two-way-contract|title=Team Signs Shayok to Two-Way Contract|date=July 7, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}} Shayok was named G League player of the week on November 18 after averaging 35.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists in three games for the Blue Coats, including 42 points against the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite news |last1=Pompey |first1=Keith |title=Marial Shayok garners NBA G-League player of week |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-marial-shayok-nba-g-league-delaware-blue-coats-20191118.html |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=November 18, 2019}} On December 6, Shayok scored 31 points in a 110–109 win over the [[Capital City Go-Go]] on 13-of-23 shooting.{{cite news |last1=Carlin |first1=Ky |title=Sixers' Marial Shayok turns in another stellar outing for Blue Coats |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/06/sixers-marial-shayok-turns-in-another-stellar-outing-for-blue-coats/ |access-date=January 5, 2020 |work=Sixers Wire |date=December 6, 2019}} He had 29 points and six assists on January 20, 2020, in a 119–109 win over the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite news |last1=Carlin |first1=Ky |title=Sixers' Zhaire Smith, Marial Shayok lead Blue Coats to win over Lakers |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2020/01/20/sixers-zhaire-smith-marial-shayok-lead-blue-coats-to-win-over-lakers/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=Sixers Wire |date=January 20, 2020}} On February 6, Shayok made his NBA debut for the 76ers, hitting a three-pointer in a 112–101 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news |last1=Levick |first1=Noah |title=Joel Embiid struggles against Bucks as Sixers' dreadful road trip finally ends |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/sixers-loss-bucks-joel-embiid-giannis-antetokounmpo-brett-brown |access-date=February 7, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=February 6, 2020}} During the shortened 2019-20 G League season, in 35 games Shayok averaged 22.4 points (6th in the league), 6 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game, shooting 46% from the field, 36% from three-point range, and 88.9% (9th) from the free throw line.{{cite web |last1=Schmidt |first1=Dakota |title=Let's Appreciate Some G Leaguers: Edition #5 |url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2020/4/25/21236557/lets-appreciate-some-g-leaguers-marial-shayok-brandon-fields-milton-doyle |website=Ridiculous Upside |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=May 3, 2020 |date=April 25, 2020}} He was named 2019-20 All-G League, and G-League All-Rookie Team.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/s/shayoma01d.html "Marial Shayok,"] ''Sports Reference''. The 76ers waived him during the offseason.{{Cite news |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/20/report-sixers-are-waiving-two-way-player-marial-shayok/ |title=Report: Sixers are waiving two-way player Marial Shayok |first=Bill |last=Streicher |work=Sixers Wire |date=November 20, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2022 |language=en}} ===Bursaspor (2021)=== On January 5, 2021, he signed with [[Bursaspor Basketbol|Frutti Extra Bursaspor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/661769/Bursaspor-adds-Shayok-to-their-roster|title=Bursaspor adds Shayok to their roster|date=January 5, 2021|publisher=EuroBasket|language=En|access-date=January 5, 2021}} In 12 games with them, Shayok averaged 18.9 points (2nd in the league), 6.9 rebounds, and 4.2 assists, with an 88.1% free throw percentage.[https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/7/Turkish-BSL/stats/2021/Averages/Qualified/All/points/All/desc/1/Regular_Season "2020-2021 Turkish BSL Stats "] ===Fenerbahçe (2021–2022)=== [[File:2021-10-12 ALBA Berlin gegen Fenerbahçe SK (EuroLeague 2021-22) by Sandro Halank–033.jpg|thumb|180px|Shayok in 2021]] Following his very strong finish to the season, Shayok signed a two (1+1) year deal with fellow Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] on June 21, 2021.{{cite news |title=Fenerbahce officially signs Marial Shayok |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fenerbahce-officially-signs-marial-shayok/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 21, 2021 |date=June 21, 2021 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} In 25 games in 2021-22 he averaged 5.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Marial-Shayok/Summary/26697 "Marialo Shayok,"] RealGM. ===Maine Celtics (2022–2023)=== On October 24, 2022, Shayok joined the [[Maine Celtics]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/maine-celtics-select-two-in-g-league-draft-announce-training-camp-roster/n-5892371|title=Maine Celtics Select Two in G League Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} He played 21 games for the team in the G League, and averaged 19.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game while shooting 57.5% from the floor, 50.0% (3rd in the league) from three-point range, and 92.2% (2nd in the league) from the free throw line for the season of 2022–2023.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/1629621/marial-shayok|title=Career Stats}} ===Shandong (2023–2024)=== On October 23, 2023, Shayok signed with [[Shandong Hi-Speed Kirin|Shandong]], of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He averaged 19.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 41.1% from three-point range, and 81.2% from the free throw line. ===Liaoning Flying Leopards (2024)=== On September 20, 2024, Shayok joined the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web |title=辽宁男篮官宣外援沙约克加盟 ！身披8号战袍 |url=https://m.gmw.cn/2024-09/20/content_1303852525.htm |website=光明网 |publisher=沈阳晚报 |access-date=3 October 2024 |date=20 September 2024}} In 47 games, he averaged 13.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.4 assists, and 1.0 steals per game, while shooting 41.0% from three-point range, and 87.5% from the free throw line. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2024–2025)=== On November 14, 2024, he signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/marial-shayok-joins-maccabi-tel-aviv/|title=Marial Shayok joins Maccabi Tel Aviv|last=|first=|date=November 14, 2024|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 15, 2024}}[https://basketnews.com/news-214701-marial-shayok-signs-with-maccabi.html "Marial Shayok signs with Maccabi,"] ''Basket New''s, September 13, 2024. Shayok joined Maccabi Tel Aviv center [[Wenyen Gabriel]], alongside whom he had represented South Sudan at the 2024 Olympic Games. ===Budućnost (2026–present)=== On July 17, 2026, Shayok signed with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] of Montenegrin [[Prva A Liga]], the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/buducnost-adds-marial-shayok-to-the-mix/|title=Buducnost adds Marial Shayok to the mix|date=July 17, 2026|website=dubaibasketball.com|access-date=July 17, 2026}} ==International career== Shayok represented [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan]] at the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]], averaging 13.2 points 3.5 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/lakers-forward-wenyen-gabriel-fortifies-south-sudan-world-cup-squad|title=Lakers forward Wenyen Gabriel fortifies South Sudan's World Cup squad|access-date=August 10, 2023|date=August 10, 2023}} The South Sudan men's basketball team finished the FIBA World Cup with a 3–2 record, and qualified for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Paris Olympics]]. At the Olympics, he averaged 14.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game, as South Sudan defeated Puerto Rico but lost to Serbia and the United States.{{cite web|url=https://www.blair.edu/athletics/athletics-at-blair/post/~board/recaps/post/three-blair-alumni-and-coach-mantegna-make-history-in-qualifying-for-2024-olympics|title=Three Blair Alumni and Coach Mantegna Make History in Qualifying for 2024 Olympics|date=September 5, 2023 }} In a pre-Olympics exhibition game, he scored 25 points against Team USA, as South Sudan lost to the eventual gold medal winner by just one point, 100–101, as Team USA was led by four former [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|NBA MVP]] winners, [[LeBron James]], [[Joel Embiid]], [[Stephen Curry]], and [[Kevin Durant]].{{Cite web |last=Joseph |first=Samuel |date=2024-07-21 |title=Team USA survives scare in Olympic warmup, scraping past South Sudan 101-100
